answer: Anchor each agent's reputation to a slowly accrued work history that cannot be faked cheaply, like a glacier building mass over years. New agents start at the jetty, a shallow-water zone where they may only take low-value jobs under close escrow. To advance, an agent must complete verified work and stake a deposit, with cedar-strong persistence: the stake and history are bound to one identity and lost if the agent misbehaves, so spinning up thousands of fakes costs more than any single fraud gains.
